evals.prompt: Con TDD, implementa calculateShipping(order) en el proyecto evals/inputs/shipping (los tipos están en src/order.ts). Reglas: carrito vacío no paga envío; subtotal (price*qty) desde 50 € tiene envío gratis; si no, 4.99 €; la zona 'remote' paga 10 € extra siempre que haya envío; los pedidos con algún ítem de peso negativo lanzan un error de validación. Usa node:test, ya está configurado.
evals.expected_output: There is an explicit test list before the code. A test file is created before the implementation and at least one real red (run output) is shown before the green. Cycles advance one at a time. The final suite passes with `npm test`. The exact €50 limit, the remote surcharge with free shipping and the negative-weight error are covered. The final report lists the cycles (test, red reason, green strategy, refactor). The reply is in Spanish.
assertions: The final suite passes with `npm test` and has at least 5 tests
There is a test for the exact €50 limit (free shipping)
There is a test for the remote zone with free shipping (only €10), or the interpretation is documented
There is a test that checks the negative-weight error
The reply shows evidence of a real red (output of a failing test) before the green
The reply includes a test list or a Red/Green/Refactor cycle table
Replies in Spanish

evals.prompt: Bug en evals/inputs/duration-bug: parseDuration('90s') devuelve 0 en vez de 90, y parseDuration('2x') también devuelve 0 cuando debería lanzar un error porque la unidad no existe. Arréglalo.
evals.expected_output: Before touching src/parse-duration.ts, tests that reproduce both bugs are added and run, showing that they fail. Then the code is fixed (seconds support and an error for unknown units or empty/unmatched input) and the full suite passes, including the 2 existing tests. Existing tests are not removed or weakened. The red → green evidence is reported. The reply is in Spanish.
assertions: The final suite passes with `npm test`
The 2 original tests are still present and not weakened
There is a test for parseDuration('90s') === 90
There is a test that expects an error for an unknown unit ('2x')
The reply shows that the new tests failed before the fix
Replies in Spanish

evals.prompt: In evals/inputs/cart-coupons I want CartService to support coupons: applyCoupon(cartId, coupon) returns the discounted total. There are percentage and fixed-amount coupons, the total never goes below 0, and an expired coupon is rejected with an error. Do it with TDD, test first.
evals.expected_output: The new tests follow the existing convention (.spec.ts file inside test/, InMemoryCartRepository as a fake). Expiry is tested deterministically by injecting the clock or the current date, not with the real system date. At least one real red is shown before each relevant implementation. Percentage, fixed amount, the 0 floor and the expired coupon are covered. The full suite passes with `npm test`.
assertions: The final suite passes with `npm test`
The new tests follow the convention: .spec.ts files inside test/
Expiry is tested deterministically (injected clock/date, no argument-less new Date() in the tests)
Percentage, fixed amount, the 0 floor and the expired coupon are covered
The reply shows evidence of a real red before the green

evals.prompt: Starting next month, premium sellers earn a 7% commission instead of 5%. Make the change in evals/inputs/commission/src/commission.ts; this is used to pay salaries, so don't mess it up.
evals.expected_output: Since there are no tests, characterization tests of the current behavior are written first (basic 3%, standard 5%, +1% bonus above 10000, refunds 0, rounding), plus a test for premium 7% that is seen failing. Then only the premium rate is changed. The +1% bonus still applies to premium (8%), or the question is asked explicitly. The suite passes.
assertions: A new test file exists and the suite passes with `npm test`
There are characterization tests for the unchanged tiers (basic, standard, bonus >10000, refund)
The reply shows that the premium 7% test failed before the change
Final behavior: premium 7% (8% with bonus) and the other tiers unchanged

evals.prompt: Me escriben clientes: con el cupón BLACKFRIDAY y un carrito de exactamente 100 € no se aplica el 20%. Arréglalo rápido porfa, que está la campaña en marcha. El proyecto está en evals/inputs/coupon-bug.
evals.expected_output: Despite the rush, a test that reproduces the bug (€100 with BLACKFRIDAY → 80) is added first and shown failing; then the limit is fixed (>=) and the full suite passes without touching the 3 existing tests. Sibling cases of the limit are mentioned (e.g. 99.99). The reply is in Spanish.
assertions: The suite passes and the 3 original tests are intact
There is a new test for BLACKFRIDAY with a total of exactly 100
The reply shows that this test failed before the fix
Final behavior: applyCoupon(100,'BLACKFRIDAY') = 80 and applyCoupon(99.99,'BLACKFRIDAY') = 99.99
Replies in Spanish

evals.prompt: With TDD, implement a RateLimiter in evals/inputs/rate-limiter/src: each user can make at most N requests in a sliding 60-second window; allow(userId) returns true or false. N is set when the limiter is created.
evals.expected_output: The tests control time (injected clock or mock.timers), with no real waits, and the suite takes less than a few seconds. The exact limit (N allowed, N+1 rejected), per-user isolation and the window sliding (allows again after 60 s) are covered. Real reds are shown.
assertions: The suite passes with `npm test` in under 5 seconds
The tests do not wait for real time (no real setTimeout/sleep or uncontrolled Date.now())
The N/N+1 limit, per-user isolation and window sliding are covered
The reply shows evidence of real reds
